reason: A staminal tube is often cylindrical, and the examples show this.
Dry fruit walls shrivel or shrink, and the examples are correct.
Wrong part. The examples are rhizome scales, not trichomes. A rule should send 'rhizome scale' to the scale, not to the shoot axis trichome.
A caudicle (the stalk of a pollinium) can be slender.
Wrong part. The examples ('equal or slightly unequal', 'unequal in most leaves') are about leaves or teeth, not the vaginant lamina. Fix the bearer.
Ellipsoid carpels are elongated round shapes, which is what PATO prolate means.
Bilobed or didymous ovaries are common, and the examples are correct.
A hypochile is a lip part and is rarely given as 'tall'. The examples may really describe the whole plant or another structure. A rule would need the head noun of the sentence.
Attachment quality is too generic. 'Veins distinct' is not about attachment, while 'lobes libres' is free versus fused. Map free or united to the specific PATO terms instead.
Wrong reading. 'Armed with stinging hairs' describes the hairs. The petiole is only the bearer of the hairs. Annotate it as petiole has part stinging trichome.
Castaneous or chestnut-brown stems are red-brown, and the examples are correct.
A suberect corolla or tube is meaningful.
Anther thecae can be equal or unequal in size.
Linear achenes are normal.
Bracts can have parallel venation.
Woody or subligneous infructescences and catkins are meaningful.
Calyx lobes can be semicircular (semiorbicular).
Wrong part. The examples describe cells seen in cross section of the leaf, not the leaf. The bearer should be the cell.
Indumentum can be persistent, and the examples are correct.
Tetragonal strobili (quadrangular in section) occur, for example in Selaginella.
Wrong reading. The examples are about a Y-mark sculpture on the spore surface, not a forked spore. The bearer should be the sculpture or the spore surface.
Gemmae can be inconspicuous.
The position of gemmae (axillary, adaxial on the costa) is a meaningful trait in bryophytes.
Pollen grains can be regular or irregular in size.
A velvety abaxial surface is valid, and the examples say 'abaxially' or 'below'.
One example says 'not fragile', and another is about modified leaves rather than the apex. A rule would need to tell the apex from the whole leaf, and handle negation.
The cottony hairs belong to the seed coat, so this is really 'seed has trichome that is cottony'. It is acceptable as a shortcut only if a rule allows it.
Cell walls are sinuous in many mosses and ferns.
The examples mix a wide pore, a widened connective and a part widening towards the base. A rule would need to name the sub-part (pore, connective) instead of the anther.

'Lateral' describes the position of the thecae. It is not a relation to another part, and 'déhiscence latérale' is about dehiscence, not position. A rule would need to separate position from dehiscence.
Calyx lobes can be partly fused to each other, as the examples show.
Corolla lobes can be attenuated, for example to the base or the apex.
Corollas can be scented or odourless, and the examples are correct.
Domatia can have cilia or hair tufts.
A rhizophore does have a length, but 'jusqu'à 4 cm de long' may describe another organ. A rule would need the head noun of the sentence.
The part is not clear, and a negated example ('n'est pas recourbé') is included. A rule would need to name the part and handle negation.
Secondary veins can be glabrous.
The part is not clear, and the examples ('base mince', 'partie inférieure canaliculée, mince') point to different organs. A rule would need to name the organ.
Petiolules can be pulvinate.
Wrong part. The examples are rhizome scales, and 'densely set' describes arrangement. It is not a quality of a trichome.
Wrong part. 'Base cordate' describes the base of a leaf or lamina. An operculum is not described this way.
Wrong reading. The examples are plain length measurements ('9–15 mm long'), so they belong to PATO length. 'Increased length' means longer than normal.
Pappus bristles and squamellae can be hispidulous.
Secretory glands can be caducous, and the examples are correct.
Seed cones can be cylindrical.
Megasporophylls (cycad scales) can be pubescent.
The shape of a perianth tube is meaningful (funnelform, campanulate, cylindrical).
Laciniate and 'quadrate or linear' describe lobes or segments, not the tunic. A rule would need to tell the tunic from its segments.
The examples are about claws and prickles, not the sepal itself. 'Indurate' means hardened.
Cauline leaves can be sessile.
Trichomes can be translucent.
Style branches can be exserted from the corolla.
Naviculate (boat-shaped) seeds are real.
Corona lobes can be toothed or dentate.
A corona or a floral tube can be tubular.
Sepals can be farinose (mealy).
Leaf lobes can be fleshy.
'Pale' is a colour intensity of the head. A rule would need the colour term it modifies, such as pale green.
Narrow filaments are meaningful.
The inside of a corolla tube can be papillate or scabrous.
